2. The facts of the case are that the petitioners are father-in-law and mother-in- law of the respondent No.2 (daughter-in-law) who are living separately from their son and his wife.
Marriage of the respondent No.2 with son of the petitioners took place on 11.05.2011 at Betul as per Hindu rites and rituals.
The marriage was solemnized in a very simple manner without there being any demand of dowry or exchange of gifts by the family members.

Immediately after the marriage it was noticed that the behaviour of the respondent No.2 towards her husband as well as the petitioners and other family members was quarrelsome and she used to create issues in the family even for small domestic work on the instigation of her parents and family members.
3.
The respondent No.2 has hardly stayed with the petitioners because the petitioner No.1 was an employee in the Hindustan Copper Ltd. and was posted at Malajkhand, Copper Project, Balaghat.
The respondent No.2 was residing with her husband at Bangalore and subsequently in Germany.
There was virtually no occasion for her to live with the petitioners.
She used to pressurize her husband to live separately and also asked not to keep any relationship with his parents.
Both the husband and wife went to Germany in the year 2014.
They returned back from Germany on 11.12.2019 and from airport at Bhopal she has not accompanied her husband and went to her parental house.
A missing report was lodged immediately by the husband being Missing Report No.74/2019 on 11.12.2019 at 12.48 P.M at P.S. Gandhinagar District Bhopal.

A legal notice was issued by the husband and immediately thereafter the FIR has been registered by the respondent No.2 against the petitioners and their son levying allegations of harassment, beating and demand of dowry.
4. Counsel appearing for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court to the documents annexed at page 53 which shows that respondent No.2 and her son are Blue Card holders in Germany.
A statement of the wife i.e. respondent No.2 recorded does not levy any specific allegations against the present applicants.
Only omnibus allegations are levied.

It is argued that once the wife i.e.,
respondent No.2 has not even resided with her parents and in her complaint all the allegations are levied against the husband.
There is no ingredients to implicate the present petitioners for commission of offence under Section 498- A and Dowry Prohibition Act.
They are old aged persons aged above 60 years who are being roped up in a false case.

It is argued that there is a tendency of roping the entire family in a false case which was being taken note off in large number of judgments.
5. Counsel for the petitioners have placed heavy reliance on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and ors. v. State of Bihar and others :
(2022) 6 SCC 599.

It would be relevant at this stage to take note of an apt observation of this Court recorded in the matter of G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held that the High Court Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72558419/
2 should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial litigation which was quashed and set aside.

Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
"there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their "young" days in chasing their cases in different courts."

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes."
6.
Counsel appearing for the respondents have vehemently opposed the contentions and supported the impugned order.
It is submitted that there are specific allegations against the petitioners that can be seen from the statement of the wife as well as the FIR.

As long as the statement is specific,
cogent and clear no interference could be made in a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR.
It is also stated that the husband of the respondent No.2 is residing in Germany and is not cooperating in the investigation in pursuance to the FIR registered against him.
7. He has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kasturi Devi and others v. State of M.P. and another : 2020(3) MPLJ 395.

8. It is held in Kasturi Devi (supra) that- "9.
Accordingly, the FIR in question cannot be quashed only on the ground that it was lodged after the receipt of service of notice of divorce petition.

On the contrary, it appears that the respondent waited with hope and belief that with passage of time,
the conduct of her in-laws may improve and this conduct of the complainant to save her matrimonial life cannot be said to be a malafide act on her part.

On the contrary,
it can be presumed that the complainant was trying to save her married life and only when she released that the things have gone beyond control / repairs, only then she lodged the FIR.
Accordingly, the FIR in question cannot be quashed on the ground that it was lodged after the institution of the divorce proceedings.

... 
15. From the plain reading of Section 498-A of IPC, it is clear that where cruelty is with a view to coerce the woman to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72558419/
3 meet such demand, then the act of the accused would be punishable under Section 498-A of IPC.

sentences.text: Section 498-A of IPC is not confined to demand of dowry only.

Accordingly, in the light of the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Rajinder Singh (Supra) and Jatinder Kumar (supra), as well as in the light of definition of curelty as provided under Section 498-A of IPC, it is held that a demand of FDR of Rs.5.00 lacs in the name of baby girl would certainly come within the purview of unlawful demand and, accordingly, the contention of the applicants that no offence would be made out under Section 498-A of IPC is hereby rejected.
So far as the delay in lodging the FIR is concerned, undisputedly, the same is not barred by time.
Thus, the FIR cannot be quashed on the ground that it was not lodged immediately.
On the contrary, it appears that the complainant must be waiting for the things to improve, but only when She realized that the things have gone beyond repairs, the FIR was lodged."

8. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
The record indicates that the marriage has taken place on 11.05.2011 between the respondent No.2 and son of the petitioners.
Thereafter, in the year 2014 both husband and wife went to Germany.
The stayed in Germany upto 2019.
On returning from Germany, the wife went to her parental house straight from the airport at Bhopal and son went to his parental house.
The allegation which has been levied in the complaint by the wife shows a series of incidences which has taken place.
There is no dispute to the proposition that wife as well as her son are Blue Card holders in Germany.
The verdict of the FIR shows that there are allegations of demand of dowry made at the time of marriage regarding harassment being caused.

Her statement is recorded in the missing complaint which was lodged by the husband on 11.12.2019. wherein she has stated that at the time of first delivery the mother-in-law has misbehaved with her and have beaten her for which she was admitted at Apollo Hospital Bangalore, which also resulted into miscarriage.
But neither there is any date mention nor there is any document to the aforesaid effect.
Even there is no complaint made by the respondent No.2 against the mother-in-law or any of the family members on any of the earlier occasions.
10. On November, 2013 a child was born.
Respondent No.2 went to Germany on 01.06.2014 along with the child, she came back in 2015 and stayed at Bangalore till 2018.
Thereafter, they again went to Germany and came back in December 2019 to Bhopal and from Bhopal airport she went to her parental house.
Thus, there is virtually no record that the respondent No.2 has even stayed with her father-in-law or mother-in-law for a considerable period after she went to Germany in the year 2014.
There is no complaint made by her at any point of time with respect to any incident prior to 2014.
Despite of there being an allegation of marpeet by the mother-in-law resulting into miscarriage, no complaint was lodged.
The documents available on record shows allegation against the husband regarding ill-treatment and demand of dowry for which the entire family is being implicated including the present petitioners.

It is not in dispute that the petitioner No.1 was in Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72558419/
4 service in Hindustan Copper Ltd. and at the relevant point of time he was posted at Malajkhand in Balaghat.

sentences.text: 11. There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has ever gone to Balaghat to stay with the father-in-law and mother-in-law.
On the contrary, when the notice of divorce was given by the husband on 06.01.2020, immediately thereafter FIR has been lodged on 07.01.2020 against the husband and other family members.
The tendency of false implication of family members in cases under Section 498-A was taken note of by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in several cases.
12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam (supra) has held as under - "11.

Having perused the relevant facts and contentions made by the Appellants and Respondents, in our considered opinion, the foremost issue which requires determination in the instant case is whether allegations made against the in-laws Appellants are in the nature of general omnibus allegations and therefore liable to be quashed?

12. Before we delve into greater detail on the nature and content of allegations made,
it becomes pertinent to mention that incorporation of section 498A of IPC was aimed at preventing cruelty committed upon a woman by her husband and her in-laws, by facilitating rapid state intervention.

However, it is equally true, that in recent times,
matrimonial litigation in the country has also increased significantly and there is a greater disaffection and friction surrounding the institution of marriage, now, more than ever.
This has resulted in an increased tendency to employ provisions such as 498A IPC as instruments to settle personal scores against the husband and his relatives.
18. Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 01.04.19, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the Appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the Appellants herein, i.e., none of the Appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the Appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution.
19. Furthermore, regarding similar allegations of harassment and demand for car as dowry made in a previous FIR.

Respondent No. 1 i.e., the State of Bihar, contends Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72558419/
5 that the present FIR pertained to offences committed in the year 2019, after assurance was given by the husband Md. Ikram before the Ld. Principal Judge Purnea, to not harass the Respondent wife herein for dowry, and treat her properly.

entities.text: Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, despite the assurances, all accused continued their demands and harassment.

It is thereby contended that the acts constitute a fresh cause of action and therefore the FIR in question herein dated 01.04.19, is distinct and independent,
and cannot be termed as a repetition of an earlier FIR dated 11.12.17."
13.
From the perusal of the aforesaid judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is apparently clear that there is a considerable increase in the matrimonial dispute in the families in the recent years.
The entire family is being roped up in criminal cases for offences under Section 498-A of IPC etc.
Tendency of false implication of the parents and other family members who are not even residing with the complainant is a general phenomenon now a days.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has gone to an extent that they have found a large number of complaints which are not even bona fide but are filed with an oblique motive.
14. There is nothing on record in the present case to show that from which period the respondent No.2 has resided with the petitioners after the year 2014.

Prior to the year 2014, there were no complaints being made by her at any point of time despite there being a specific allegation made in the present complaint regarding beating by the mother-in-law resulting into miscarriage.

15. In the absence of any specific allegations against the present petitioners, no relief can be extended to the complainant to continue with the prosecution against the petitioners who happens to be the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the respondent No.2.

In absence of any material that could be brought to the notice of this court by the respondent-counsel the registration of FIR based upon the complaint against the father-in-law and mother-in-law is unsustainable.
16. This court is aware of the fact that the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are to be used sparingly and with great caution.
But it can always be used to quash the criminal proceedings to avoid any abuse or process of law.

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a landmark judgment in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal : 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 has laid down certain guidelines which were subsequently reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment passed in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra & others : 2021 SCC Online SC 315 wherein certain guidelines have been framed certain guidelines for consideration of cases for quashment of FIR especially in paragraph 80 which reads as under :-
"80.

Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.

It would be premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts Ramrao Phate vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72558419/
7 that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

sentences.text: After investigation, if the investigating officer finds that there is no substance in the application made by the complainant, the investigating officer may file an appropriate report/summary before the learned Magistrate which may be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with the known procedure;
x i i i )
The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be more cautious.
It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;

xiv) However, at the same time, the court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self-restraint imposed by law, more particularly the parameters laid down by this Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur (supra) and Bhajan Lal (supra), has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/complaint;
x v )

When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged accused and the court when it exercises the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether the allegations in the FIR disclose commission of a cognizable offence or not.

The court is not required to consider on merits whether or not the merits of the allegations make out a cognizable offence and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR;
xvi) The aforesaid parameters would be applicable and/or the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered by the High Court while passing an interim order in a quashing petition in exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

However,
an interim order of stay of investigation during the pendency of the quashing petition can be passed with circumspection.
Such an interim order should not require to be passed routinely, casually and/or mechanically.

Normally, when the investigation is in progress and the facts are hazy and the entire evidence/material is not before the High Court, the High Court should restrain itself from passing the interim order of not to arrest or ''no coercive steps to be adopted and the accused should be relegated to apply for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. before the competent court.

sentences.text: Once the Court after going through the material placed before it arrived at a conclusion that no offence is made out against the parties can permit to continue the criminal prosecution is amounting to abuse of the process of law.

19. In the present case, this Court has already arrived at a conclusion that there are no allegations against the mother-in-law and father-in-law causing harassment, beating or any demand of dowry after the year 2014.
And prior to the year 2014 no complaints were made.
The FIR has been lodged only after returning from Germany that too after lodging of the missing complaint by the husband.
The respondent No.2 wife has not even chosen to go to the matrimonial house after returning back from Germany.
The order sheets of this case shows that the matter was sent for mediation.
The husband has made an effort to appear through video conferencing as he is residing in Germany.

But,
the wife has refused for taking up a mediation proceeding and has asked for physical presence of the husband.
This itself goes to show that the wife herself has not cooperated in the mediation proceedings.
20. As far as registration of case against the husband is concerned, this Court in the present case is not concerned with the FIR lodged against the husband.
It is only dealing with the criminal case being registered against the father-in-law and mother-in-law.
21. Under these circumstances, the criminal prosecution lodged against the father-in-law and mother-in-law (petitioners) deserves to be and is hereby quashed.
The respondent-State is expected to take all possible efforts to get the investigation completed in the matter within the stipulated time against the husband.

Parties to bear their own costs.
22.
In the result, the petition is allowed and the proceedings pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class Betul, District Betul as RCT No.588 of 2021 against the petitioners are hereby quashed.
